scope.title: Evidence collection for 'Generative Realities / Trends 2026' analysis
scope.description: Collect and curate evidence to support analysis of consumer and brand trends related to generative AI, AI-enabled influencers/agents, slow/analog counter-trends, and fandom-driven experiences as described in Trends 2026.
scope.jurisdiction: Global (primary focus: US, UK, China, India, Japan, Brazil, Spain)
include: Published reports and whitepapers (PDF, DOCX) describing trends, methodologies, and survey results
Quantitative datasets and survey results (CSV, XLSX) used to support trend claims
Campaign case studies and creative assets (images, video, copy) demonstrating brand work
Press releases, industry news articles, and regulatory guidance relevant to AI-generated content and disclosures
Academic papers and expert commentaries on parasocial relationships, AI agents, and media effects
Platform policy documents and takedown / moderation reports where relevant
exclude: Unnecessary PII (names, personal identifiers) not required for trend-level analysis
Internal draft notes not intended for external use unless explicitly permitted
Low-value social media noise (single social posts without engagement or provenance) unless they are viral/representative examples
dataTypes: metadata and provenance records (timestamps, source URLs, content hashes)

high: Primary reports and datasets that underpin trend claims
Campaign performance data and case studies with metrics
medium: Industry press coverage and platform policy updates
low: Ephemeral social posts unless they are demonstrably impactful or viral

deliverables: Curated evidence repository organized by source and data type
Annotated index mapping each item to the trend assertion(s) it supports
Summary brief with cited evidence and confidence levels for each key claim

retentionAndAccess.accessRestrictions: Sensitive datasets requiring access controls; redact PII before wider sharing

scope.notes: Scope defined to support an EvidencePack for Trends 2026 — Generative Realities. Example source used as framing: Dentsu Creative Trends 2026
